name: Jump squat
form_cues: Sit back to a quarter or half squat, arms swinging back.
Drive through the whole foot and jump straight up.
Land softly and sink straight into the next rep.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged with a loud thud
Knees caving in on take-off or landing
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Pause squat jump
form_cues: Lower to a half squat and hold still for 2–3 seconds.
Explode straight up without dipping first.
Stick the landing, reset, then repeat.
common_mistakes: Dipping before the jump, which defeats the pause
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Trains starting strength by removing the stretch-shortening cycle.

name: Countermovement jump
form_cues: Dip quickly into a quarter squat while swinging arms back.
Throw arms up hard and extend hips, knees and ankles together.
Reach as high as you can, then land quietly.
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Rest fully between reps; quality over fatigue. Jump-and-reach against a wall to measure progress.

name: Tuck jump
form_cues: Jump straight up from a quick dip.
Pull your knees up toward your chest at the top.
Untuck before landing and land softly on the balls of your feet.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward instead of jumping vertically
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Pike jump
form_cues: Jump straight up with a strong arm drive.
Lift straight legs forward and reach hands toward toes.
Drop legs back under you before you land.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees instead of piking
safety: Needs good hamstring flexibility; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Frog jump
form_cues: Start in a wide, deep squat with fingers near the floor.
Jump up and forward, swinging arms overhead.
Land back in the deep squat and go again.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom
safety: Only squat as deep as you can with a flat back; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: 180-degree jump squat
form_cues: Squat down and swing arms to start the turn.
Jump and rotate 180 degrees in the air.
Land facing the other way in a soft squat, then reverse.
common_mistakes: Twisting the knees on landing instead of turning fully in the air
safety: Land with feet and knees pointing the same way; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Split jump
form_cues: Start in a lunge, chest up, front knee over mid-foot.
Jump up and switch legs in the air.
Land softly back into a lunge and go straight away.
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Broad jump
form_cues: Swing arms back and hinge at the hips.
Drive arms forward and jump as far out as you can.
Land in a quarter squat and hold the landing for a second.
common_mistakes: Falling forward or backward on landing
Jumping too high instead of out
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Measure distance from toes to heels to track progress.

name: Consecutive broad jumps
form_cues: Do one broad jump, then rebound straight into the next.
Spend as little time on the ground as possible.
Keep the arm swing rhythmic and powerful.
safety: Use a flat, non-slip surface; land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Single-leg broad jump
form_cues: Stand on one leg, hinge and swing arms back.
Jump forward off one leg as far as you can.
Land on the same leg and hold it for two seconds.
common_mistakes: Jumping further than you can control
safety: Master two-leg landings first; stop if knee feels unstable.
notes: Common return-to-sport hop test.

name: Lateral bound
form_cues: Load on one leg and push hard sideways off it.
Jump as far as you can to the side.
Land on the opposite leg and stick it for a second.
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Make it continuous for conditioning; stick each landing for strength and control.

name: Alternate-leg bounding
form_cues: Push off one leg and drive the other knee forward and up.
Swing the opposite arm hard with each stride.
Cover as much ground per bound as you can, landing under hips.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a run with short strides
Landing heel-first far ahead of the body
safety: Use grass or a track; build up volume slowly to protect shins and Achilles.

name: Straight-leg bound
form_cues: Keep knees nearly straight and stay tall.
Sweep each leg down and back, striking under your hips.
Pull the ground behind you with quick, active feet.
common_mistakes: Reaching the foot out in front
safety: Warm up well first; stop if you feel any hamstring tightness.
notes: Sprint drill that teaches a fast, backward-pulling foot strike.

name: Pogo jumps
form_cues: Stand tall with almost-straight knees.
Bounce off the balls of your feet using only your ankles.
Keep ground contact quick and stiff, like a spring.
safety: Build up slowly if you have Achilles or calf issues.
notes: Great warm-up for running and jumping; builds ankle stiffness.

name: Single-leg hop
form_cues: Balance on one leg with a soft knee.
Hop forward a short distance and land on the same foot.
Keep the knee over the toes and hips level.
common_mistakes: Hip dropping on the free-leg side
safety: Stop if the landing knee wobbles or hurts.

name: Lateral line hops
form_cues: Stand beside a line with feet together.
Hop side to side over it as fast as you can.
Stay on the balls of your feet with quick, light contacts.
safety: Use a non-slip surface; ease in if ankles are stiff.

name: Forward-backward line hops
form_cues: Stand behind a line with feet together.
Hop forward and back over it quickly.
Keep knees soft and contacts short.
safety: Use a non-slip surface.
notes: Do single-leg for more challenge.

name: Single-leg lateral hop
form_cues: Stand on one leg beside a line.
Hop sideways over it and back on the same leg.
Land quietly with the knee tracking over the toes.
safety: Stop if the ankle or knee feels unstable.

name: Snap down
form_cues: Rise onto your toes with arms overhead.
Snap arms down and drop fast into an athletic quarter squat.
Freeze in the landing: chest up, hips back, knees over toes.
common_mistakes: Too deep and slow a drop
safety: Teaches safe landing mechanics; keep the drop quick but controlled.
notes: Use as a warm-up before any jumping session.

name: A-skip
form_cues: Skip forward, driving one knee to hip height.
Pull the foot down to strike under your hips.
Opposite arm drives with each knee; stay tall.
common_mistakes: Reaching the foot out in front
safety: Use a flat surface and warm up first.
notes: Classic sprint mechanics drill; walk it as an A-march to learn it.

name: B-skip
form_cues: Start like an A-skip, knee up to hip height.
Extend the lower leg forward, then paw it down and back.
Strike under your hips and keep a steady rhythm.
common_mistakes: Kicking the leg out and landing in front
safety: Stop if you feel hamstring tightness; warm up first.
notes: Teaches the active pull-back of the foot used in sprinting.

name: Power skip
form_cues: Skip, pushing hard off the ground for height.
Drive the knee and opposite arm up together.
Land softly and go straight into the next skip.
common_mistakes: Skipping low and fast instead of high
safety: Use a non-slip surface and build up gradually.
notes: Do it for distance instead of height as a variation.

name: Carioca
form_cues: Move sideways, crossing the trail leg in front then behind.
Rotate the hips while the shoulders stay square.
Stay on the balls of your feet and speed up as you get it.
common_mistakes: Turning the shoulders with the hips
Tripping over crossing feet by going too fast too soon
safety: Start slowly; use a flat, clear surface.
notes: Great dynamic warm-up for field and court sports.

name: Incline plyo push-up
form_cues: Hands on a wall, bench or counter, body straight.
Lower quickly, then push hard so your hands leave the surface.
Catch yourself with soft elbows and go again.
safety: Use a stable surface that will not slide.
notes: The higher the hands, the easier it is.

name: Kneeling plyo push-up
form_cues: Kneel with hands under shoulders and a straight line knees to head.
Lower, then push explosively so hands leave the floor.
Land with soft elbows and flow into the next rep.
safety: Use a mat for the knees; stop if wrists hurt.

name: Plyo push-up
form_cues: Start in a strong plank, hands under shoulders.
Lower under control, then push hard so hands leave the floor.
Land with soft elbows and go straight into the next rep.
safety: Warm up wrists and shoulders; stop if you land with pain.

name: Clap push-up
form_cues: Lower to just above the floor with a tight body.
Explode up high enough to clap once.
Get hands back under shoulders and land softly.
common_mistakes: Not getting enough height and landing on the face
safety: Practise on a soft mat; only progress once plyo push-ups are high and controlled.

name: Wall drill
form_cues: Lean into a wall at about 45 degrees, hands on it.
Hold one knee up, toe pulled up, body in a straight line.
Switch legs explosively, striking down under your hips.
common_mistakes: Bending at the hips instead of leaning as a straight line
Feet drifting forward under the wall
safety: Wear shoes with grip so your feet do not slip.
notes: Teaches the body angle and leg action of acceleration.

name: Acceleration sprint
form_cues: Start from a split stance, leaning forward.
Push the ground back hard with powerful, full strides.
Rise gradually to upright over the first 10–15 m.
safety: Warm up thoroughly; rest 1–2 min between reps to stay fast.
notes: Track times if you can; stop when speed drops.

name: Falling start sprint
form_cues: Stand tall and lean forward from the ankles as one straight line.
When you feel you will fall, explode into a sprint.
Keep the lean for the first few strong steps.
common_mistakes: Stepping out too far in front of the body
safety: Warm up first; use a surface with good grip.

name: Flying sprint
form_cues: Build up over 20–30 m to near top speed.
Sprint the marked zone at full speed, running tall.
Stay relaxed in face and shoulders; strike under your hips.
safety: Only do these fresh and fully warmed up; hamstring strains happen at top speed.
notes: Trains maximum velocity; rest 3+ min between reps.

name: Hill sprint
form_cues: Lean into the hill from the ankles, not the waist.
Drive knees forward and pump arms hard.
Walk back down to recover fully between reps.
common_mistakes: Shortening stride and arm swing as you tire
safety: Choose a moderate, even slope; the incline is easier on hamstrings than flat sprints.
notes: A treadmill set to a steep incline can substitute.

name: Broad jump into sprint
form_cues: Do one maximal broad jump.
Land in an athletic stance with a forward lean.
Immediately sprint out 10 m, pushing hard on the first steps.
common_mistakes: Stalling or standing up after the landing
safety: Land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.
notes: Links jumping power to acceleration.

name: Backpedal to sprint
form_cues: Backpedal low with weight on the balls of your feet.
On the cue or line, open the hips and turn.
Accelerate forward hard for 10 m.
safety: Use a clear, flat area; start slowly.

name: Lateral shuffle
form_cues: Get into a low athletic stance, chest up.
Push off the trail leg and step sideways without crossing feet.
Keep your hips low and level.
safety: Use a flat, non-slip surface.

name: Dot drill
form_cues: Mark five dots like the five on a die.
Hop between dots in the set pattern as fast as you can.
Stay on the balls of your feet with quick contacts.
safety: Use tape on a non-slip floor.
notes: Do two-foot, then single-foot patterns.

name: Shuttle run
form_cues: Sprint to the line and touch it with your hand.
Drop your hips and plant the outside foot to turn.
Push off hard and accelerate back.
common_mistakes: Rounding wide turns instead of planting
safety: Wear grippy shoes on a non-slip surface.
notes: No cones? Use court or field lines. No gear id for cones, so req is empty.

name: 5-10-5 pro agility drill
form_cues: Start straddling the middle line in a low stance.
Sprint 5 m one way, touch, then 10 m the other way.
Touch and sprint 5 m back through the middle.
common_mistakes: Crossing the feet on the first step
safety: Use a grippy surface; rest fully between timed reps.
notes: Standard combine test (5-10-5 yards); metres work fine.

name: T-drill
form_cues: Sprint forward 10 m to the middle cone.
Shuffle 5 m left, 10 m right, 5 m back to the middle.
Backpedal to the start, staying low throughout.
safety: Use a flat, non-slip surface.
notes: Cones laid out in a T; no gear id for cones, so req is empty.

name: L-drill
form_cues: Set three cones in an L, 5 m apart.
Sprint out and back, then go round the far cone in a figure eight.
Stay low and tight round the cones; sprint home.
safety: Use a grippy surface; rest fully between reps.
notes: NFL combine 3-cone drill.

name: Box drill
form_cues: Set four cones in a 5 m square.
Sprint forward, shuffle sideways, backpedal, then shuffle back.
Stay low and keep your hips facing forward.
common_mistakes: Crossing the feet in the shuffle
safety: Use a non-slip surface.
notes: Trains changes between forward, lateral and backward movement.

name: Zig-zag cone drill
form_cues: Set cones 3–5 m apart in a zig-zag.
Sprint to each cone and cut sharply off the outside foot.
Lower your hips before each cut.
common_mistakes: Leaning the body the wrong way on the cut
safety: Use a grippy surface; build up speed gradually.

name: Agility ladder: one foot in each
form_cues: Run through, placing one foot in each square.
Stay on the balls of your feet, arms pumping.
Speed up only as long as you stay clean.
common_mistakes: Looking straight down the whole time
progressions: Agility ladder: two feet in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: two feet in each
form_cues: Step both feet into each square, one after the other.
Keep steps short, light and fast.
Drive arms in rhythm with your feet.
regressions: Agility ladder: one foot in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: lateral in-in-out-out
form_cues: Face the side of the ladder.
Step in, in, then out, out, moving down one square each time.
Keep your hips low and facing forward.
regressions: Agility ladder: two feet in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Icky shuffle
form_cues: Step in-in, then out to the side, moving forward each square.
Alternate the outside step from side to side.
Stay light and rhythmic, eyes up.
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: hopscotch
form_cues: Hop with both feet into a square, then land one foot either side of the next.
Alternate in and out all the way down.
Keep contacts quick and quiet.
regressions: Agility ladder: two feet in each
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder: single-leg hops
form_cues: Hop on one foot into each square.
Land softly on the ball of the foot, knee slightly bent.
Keep the hip level and the knee over the toes.
common_mistakes: Hopping too far and losing control
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Agility ladder crossover
form_cues: Move sideways along the ladder.
Cross the trail foot over into each square, then step out.
Turn the hips, keep the shoulders square.
safety: Lay the ladder flat on a non-slip surface so it cannot slide.
notes: Agility ladder has no gear id, so req is empty; tape on the floor works too.

name: Hurdle hops
form_cues: Line up 4–6 low hurdles about a stride apart.
Jump over each with both feet, tucking knees slightly.
Rebound quickly off each landing, staying tall.
common_mistakes: Clipping hurdles by not lifting the knees
safety: Use collapsible hurdles or cones that fall over if clipped.
notes: No gear id for hurdles; req is empty.

name: Band-resisted sprint
form_cues: Loop the band round your waist with a partner holding behind.
Lean forward and drive hard with powerful steps.
Keep strong arm drive and a straight body line.
common_mistakes: Partner pulling so hard your form breaks
safety: Check the band for wear and anchor it securely.
notes: Can also be done in place against an anchored band.

name: Parachute sprint
form_cues: Clip the chute on and start with a strong forward lean.
Sprint hard so the chute opens behind you.
Keep your form tall and relaxed once the chute fills.
safety: Use only in open space with no wind gusts that could yank you.
notes: No gear id for a speed chute; req is empty.

name: Medicine ball chest pass
form_cues: Stand in an athletic stance, ball at your chest.
Step and throw the ball hard and straight at the wall.
Catch on the rebound and go again with control.
common_mistakes: Throwing with only the arms and no leg drive
safety: Use a ball that bounces (not a slam ball) for wall throws; keep your face clear on the rebound.
notes: 3–5 kg suits most people.

name: Rotational medicine ball throw
form_cues: Stand side-on to a wall, ball at the back hip.
Drive the back hip round and let the arms follow.
Release hard into the wall and catch the rebound.
common_mistakes: Throwing with the arms instead of the hips
safety: Use a soft or rebounding ball; check the wall can take impact.
notes: Great for golf, tennis, baseball and combat sports.

name: Medicine ball shot-put throw
form_cues: Hold the ball at your shoulder, side-on to the wall.
Rotate the hips and push the ball out with one arm.
Follow through fully and reset each rep.
common_mistakes: Pushing with the arm before the hips turn
safety: Keep the wrist behind the ball; use a soft ball.

name: Medicine ball slam
form_cues: Lift the ball overhead, rising onto your toes.
Slam it down hard in front of your feet using your abs and lats.
Squat to pick it up with a flat back.
common_mistakes: Using a ball that bounces back into the face
Rounding the back to pick it up
safety: Use a dead (non-bounce) slam ball and keep the face away from the bounce.

name: Rotational medicine ball slam
form_cues: Lift the ball overhead, then rotate towards one side.
Slam it down outside your foot, pivoting the back foot.
Pick up and alternate sides.
common_mistakes: Twisting through the lower back only
safety: Use a dead slam ball; keep the spine long.

name: Wall ball
form_cues: Hold the ball at your chest and squat to parallel.
Drive up and throw it to a target about 3 m high.
Catch it and go straight into the next squat.
safety: Use a soft wall ball; stand about an arm's length from the wall.
notes: CrossFit standard: 9 kg / 6 kg to 3 m / 2.7 m.

name: Overhead backward medicine ball throw
form_cues: Hold the ball low between your legs, hips hinged.
Explode through the hips and throw the ball up and back over your head.
Let arms follow straight through.
safety: Make sure the area behind you is completely clear.
notes: Excellent hip-extension power drill; measure throw distance.

name: Underhand forward medicine ball throw
form_cues: Hinge with the ball held low between your legs.
Drive hips forward and throw the ball out and up.
Let the throw pull you into a step or jump forward.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom
safety: Throw into open space away from people.

name: Overhead medicine ball throw
form_cues: Stand or kneel with the ball overhead, arms long.
Brace the abs and pull the ball forward hard.
Release in front of the head into a wall or partner.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to wind up
safety: Keep ribs down; use a soft ball for wall throws.

name: Dumbbell jump squat
form_cues: Hold light dumbbells at your sides or a kettlebell at your chest.
Dip to a quarter squat and jump as high as you can.
Land softly and reset before the next rep.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy so jumps barely leave the floor
safety: Keep the load light (10–30% of body weight); land softly with knees soft and tracking over toes; skip if you have acute knee or ankle pain.

name: Dumbbell split jump
form_cues: Hold light dumbbells at your sides in a lunge stance.
Jump up, switching legs in the air.
Land softly in a lunge with the front knee over the foot.
common_mistakes: Using weights that are too heavy
safety: Keep loads light and stop when landings get sloppy.

name: Box jump
form_cues: Stand a foot from the box, swing arms back and dip.
Jump and land softly on the box in a quarter squat.
Stand tall, then step down rather than jumping off.
common_mistakes: Choosing a box so high you land in a deep squat
safety: Use a stable box; step down to protect Achilles and knees.
notes: Height of jump, not box, is the goal.

name: Seated box jump
form_cues: Sit on a bench facing the box, feet flat.
Swing arms and explode up off the seat onto the box.
Land softly and step down.
safety: Start with a low box; step down after each rep.
notes: Removes the countermovement to build starting strength.

name: Depth drop
form_cues: Step off a low box, do not jump off.
Land on both feet at once in an athletic quarter squat.
Freeze the landing for two seconds.
common_mistakes: Stepping off a box too high
safety: Start at 30–45 cm; stop if knees ache.
notes: Teaches landing before you add depth jumps.

name: Depth jump
form_cues: Step off a low box and land on both feet.
Spend as little time on the ground as possible.
Rebound straight up as high as you can.
common_mistakes: Box too high so you cannot rebound quickly
Jumping off the box instead of stepping
safety: Advanced shock drill: do it fresh, low volume, with a 30–60 cm box and good landing mechanics first.
notes: Rest 1–2 min between reps.

name: Single-leg box jump
form_cues: Stand on one leg facing a low box.
Swing arms and jump onto the box off one leg.
Land on the same leg, stabilise, step down.
safety: Use a low box; step down every rep.

name: Lateral box jump
form_cues: Stand side-on to a low box.
Dip and jump sideways onto it, landing with both feet.
Step down and repeat, switching sides each set.
safety: Start with a low box; step down each rep.

name: Power step-up
form_cues: Place one foot fully on a knee-height box.
Drive through that foot to jump up, swinging the other knee high.
Land softly with the same foot on the box and repeat.
common_mistakes: Box too high so the hip sinks below the knee
safety: Use a stable box that won't tip; keep the working knee over the foot.
notes: Alternating version switches feet in the air.

name: Depth push-up
form_cues: Hold a plank with hands on two low boxes.
Drop hands to the floor between them, landing with soft elbows.
Push explosively back up onto the boxes.
safety: Only attempt once clap push-ups are solid; keep the boxes low.

name: Trap bar jump
form_cues: Stand in the bar, grab the handles, chest up.
Dip quickly and jump as high as you can.
Land softly with knees bent, absorbing the bar.
safety: Use 10–30% of your deadlift; land with soft knees and a flat back.
notes: A safer loaded jump than barbell jump squats.

name: Sled sprint
form_cues: Attach the harness at the waist and lean forward.
Sprint with powerful pushes and strong arm drive.
Keep the load light enough to keep good sprint form.
common_mistakes: Loading so heavy it becomes a walk
safety: Use a harness at the waist and a light load; rest fully between reps.
notes: Light (10–20% body weight) for speed; heavier for acceleration strength.

name: Sled push
form_cues: Grip the poles with arms extended and lean at 45 degrees.
Drive with short, powerful steps through the balls of the feet.
Keep your back flat and hips low.
safety: Use a lane with good grip; stop if back rounds.
notes: Light and fast for power; heavy for strength and conditioning.
